screen1-a1.where: Top left corner, three short stacked lines beside the word "messenger".
screen1-a1.expectation: I do not know. Three short lines stacked on top of one another. Perhaps a list of some kind, but I could not say what would open.
screen1-a1.cue: Nothing but the three lines. There is no word beside them.

first_pass.why: Three lines is not a symbol I know the meaning of, and I cannot learn it. I would leave it alone rather than press something when I cannot say what it does.
first_pass.solution: Put a word under it, such as "Menu", or better, say what is in it.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "Three lines is not a symbol I know the meaning of, and I cannot learn it. I would leave it alone rather than press something when I cannot say what it does." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); press the box tagged a1 (Top left corner, three short stacked lines beside the word "messenger".), look at what appears, then come back with the arrow at the top left or the phone's Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "I do not know. Three short lines stacked on top of one another. Perhaps a list of some kind, but I could not say what would open."), or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears matches what you expected and you can tell what it did
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the three lines at the top left of the first screen. A panel slid out from the left with a list of plain words: Communities, Message requests, Archive, Friend requests, Subscriptions, Facebook Reels, Facebook Events, Facebook Dating, with my name at the top. It was a list, as I half guessed. The panel has no heading of its own. (One run, from the first screen; the same three lines sit at the top of the People and Notifications pages, and I record the same outcome for them.)

screen1-a1.closing_comment: What it opens is a list of mostly plain words, so once I am in there I can manage. But the three lines themselves still tell me nothing, and next time I will not remember that this is where those things are kept.

screen1-a2.where: Top right, a square with a pencil over it.
screen1-a2.expectation: I suppose I would write something. A pencil on a square sheet suggests writing, but writing what, and to whom, I cannot say.
screen1-a2.cue: The little pencil drawn over a square.

first_pass.why: A pencil means writing, but nothing tells me whether this is a new letter, a note, or changing something already there. I would have to press it and find out.
first_pass.solution: A word beside it: "New message".

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "A pencil means writing, but nothing tells me whether this is a new letter, a note, or changing something already there. I would have to press it and find out." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); press the box tagged a2 (Top right, a square with a pencil over it.), look at what appears, then come back with the arrow at the top left or the phone's Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "I suppose I would write something. A pencil on a square sheet suggests writing, but writing what, and to whom, I cannot say."), or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears matches what you expected and you can tell what it did
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the square with the pencil. A page opened with the heading "New message" and "To: Type a name or group", with New story, New note, Group chat and a list of people underneath. (One run; same button on every first-screen picture.)

screen1-a2.closing_comment: It did what I guessed, writing a new message, and the page names itself clearly. I still would rather the button said "New message" before I press it.

screen1-a3.where: Top right corner, the Facebook "f" in a black circle.
screen1-a3.expectation: It would take me to Facebook.
screen1-a3.cue: The Facebook "f" in the circle. I have seen that mark for many years.

first_pass.why: That mark has been the same for a long time and I know it as Facebook.

screen1-a4.where: The blue strip across the top: "Notifications are currently off. Tap to turn on."
screen1-a4.expectation: It would turn on notifications, so that I am told when a message comes in.
screen1-a4.cue: The words on the blue strip: "Notifications are currently off. Tap to turn on."

first_pass.why: It says exactly what is off and what pressing it will do.

screen1-a5.where: The long grey box with a magnifying glass: "Ask Meta AI or search".
screen1-a5.expectation: I would type a name in here to find someone. I do not know what "Meta AI" is, so I would ignore that part.
screen1-a5.cue: The magnifying glass and the words "Ask Meta AI or search".

first_pass.why: "Search" I understand, but "Meta AI" is a name I do not know and cannot learn. I am not sure whether I would be searching my messages or asking some machine a question. And the words will vanish the moment I start to type.
first_pass.solution: Just say "Search for a person or a message" and keep that wording above the box while I type.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: ""Search" I understand, but "Meta AI" is a name I do not know and cannot learn. I am not sure whether I would be searching my messages or asking some machine ..." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); tap the box tagged a5 (The long grey box with a magnifying glass: "Ask Meta AI or search".), type something you would really put there, watch the screen while you type, then delete what you typed without sending anything
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: while you type you can no longer tell what the box is for, or it does not take what you expected (you said: "I would type a name in here to find someone. I do not know what "Meta AI" is, so I would ignore that part.")
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen keeps showing what the box is for and it takes what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I tapped the grey bar. A search page opened with a list of suggested people. I typed "Marco". The grey words "Ask Meta AI or search" vanished as I typed, but Marco Peralta came up at once, with words across the top such as People, Messages and Groups. An "Ask" button also appeared at the right of the box, which I did not touch. I deleted what I typed. (One run; same bar on every first-screen picture.)

screen1-a5.closing_comment: It found the person I typed, which is what I wanted, and the groupings help me. The instructions still vanish once I type, and the "Ask" button and "Meta AI" mean nothing to me.
